definitions: A topographic surname from Middle English.
A unisex given name from English.

blocks.text: A thicket is a very dense stand of trees or tall shrubs, often dominated by only one or a few species to the exclusion of all others. They may be formed by species that shed large numbers of highly viable seeds that are able to germinate in the shelter of the maternal plants.
Brier is an English topographic surname. It was used for people who lived near briar patches or as a nickname for a prickly person. Notable people with the surname include:

items: Glenn W. Brier, United States statistician and weather forecaster
Joe Brier, British sprinter and brother of Hannah
Kathy Brier, American actor and singer
Sabrina Brier, American actress, comedian, and influencer
Tom Brier, American ragtime composer and pianist, child prodigy

blocks.text: Briar is an open-source software communication technology, intended to provide secure and resilient peer-to-peer communications with no centralized servers and minimal reliance on external infrastructure. Messages can be transmitted through Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, over the internet via Tor or removable storage, such as USB sticks. All communication is end-to-end encrypted. Relevant content is stored in encrypted form on participating devices. Long-term plans for the project include support for distributed applications such as crisis mapping and collaborative document editing.
